events.title: PortWatch reports the private build omonkey taken down, hours after its developer's reported letter from Rockstar
events.note: PortWatch reports the private build omonkey taken down, hours after its developer's reported letter from Rockstar  PortWatch removed omonkey from its board at 18:19 UTC , saying on its owner's word that the private build has been taken down. Its code was never public, so there is nothing to check, and no notice or statement has been published. VGTimes reported earlier today that its developer said he had received a letter from Rockstar and stopped streaming. Its row here keeps its last reported status. With ztrx's repository and account gone since about 17:00 UTC , two builds of victory-fork's code have gone dark today with no reason published. The mark published with the estimate asks for a takedown notice that names VIctory, victory-fork or a build of it, and GitHub's list holds none, so the estimate is unchanged. Both cases will weigh in its next review. vilocity's README now gives 4 to 8 frames a second in the first room on an RTX 5080, up from 3 to 7. klbf-lab's README adds that it never publishes a build that crashed in its own tests and that its 77-minute session was stopped by choice. XCL merged 28 pull requests into its main branch with its status row unchanged.     18:13  25 Nov
events.analysis: 涉及权利人或平台措施；以公开原始通知为准。

events.title: VI-BR-PORT joins the table near the top, and ruff-lab logs 21.8 minutes without player control
events.note: VI-BR-PORT joins the table near the top, and ruff-lab logs 21.8 minutes without player control  VI-BR-PORT, a fork of victory-fork for NVIDIA cards with 8 GB, joins at stage 6. Its README, in Portuguese, reports control, the HUD and the pause menu working at 4 to 7 frames a second at 1080p on an RTX 4060 Ti, sessions of an hour without losing the graphics device, and all 25,758 of the game's shaders translating on that card, with everything in shadow black. These are its own figures and estimates from one machine. The length of those sessions places it 4th, 2 steps short of the playable bar. ruff-lab's results log now holds a session of 21.8 minutes without a crash at 3.23 frames a second on average on an 8 GB Radeon RX 6600 XT with a hard disk. It says player movement does not work yet because of a controller input problem, so it stays at stage 5. vilocity's README says its rainbow glitter is gone and every shader now translates, still at 3 to 7 frames a second. five-star-recomp's status page says boots now stay 5 to 7 minutes in the world, with the lit picture still wrong. News check: other trackers repeat that ztrx's repository and account are gone, and none gives a reason. GitHub's list holds no new notice, and neither Rockstar nor Take-Two has commented since the build leaked.     17:50  25 Nov
events.analysis: 涉及运行稳定性；需要核对持续时长及是否发生崩溃。

events.title: victory-fork measures 4.5 frames a second in a play session, and the estimate moves back to under two days
events.note: victory-fork measures 4.5 frames a second in a play session, and the estimate moves back to under two days  victory-fork's README ( 17:28 UTC ) reports a 370-second play session at 4.5 frames a second on average, against 10.3 standing still. Half the time goes to frames of about 490 milliseconds in which the card sits idle, because the game maps every streamed texture page itself, about 850 pages in a frame that streams. Two attempts to cut that cost were taken back out, one after faces came out black or red. Its speed lane now reads from its two play sessions, 4.5 on its own RTX 4070 and 7.6 on an RTX 4090 in a pull request, and it stays 3rd. The estimate moves back by three quarters of a day, to midday on Fri 27 Nov. The best averages from sessions of play are 7.6 to 8.6 against the 20 the bar asks for, and the figures of 10 or more came from the lightest scenes. This replaces the check published for 22:00 UTC , and the estimate's note gives the next marks. PortWatch reported at 17:26 UTC that ztrx's repository and the account that published it are both gone, with no takedown notice published. events.note: ztrx's repository stops answering, Belobug's fork reaches 5 to 7 frames a second, and the estimate is reviewed and held  ztrx's repository has not answered since 16:57 UTC , in three checks over 25 minutes while every other tracked repository answered, the last of them after GitHub closed its incident at 16:52 UTC . GitHub's published list holds no notice that names it and PortWatch still lists it, so the reason is not known: a repository made private, deleted or disabled looks the same from outside. Its row keeps its last reported status, without a link. Belobug's fork now reports 5 to 7 frames a second on a Radeon RX 9070 XT, from 3 to 5: 5.4 to 6.7 standing still in a scene of 8,400 draws, less while driving. Its README puts the gain down to letting the game's submissions return before the card is done and to using game memory in place instead of copying it. events.title: VIctory's own README now says you can get into the game, and victory-fork qualifies its 10 frames a second
events.note: VIctory's own README now says you can get into the game, and victory-fork qualifies its 10 frames a second  VIctory's README ( 16:51 UTC ) now opens with "Not playable yet, but you can get into the game". It says the intro cutscene plays and the opening mission is reached with the graphics fully displayed at about 1 frame a second on a Radeon RX 6700 XT: textured and lit, without ray-traced shadows or indirect light. Its picture lane moves from step 1 to step 2. victory-fork's maintainer added a limit at 16:54 UTC to the figures reported here at 15:38 and 16:19 UTC : the 9.6 and 10.3 frames a second are for the scene standing still. While the camera moves the game streams assets, and about half the time goes to frames of about 490 milliseconds in which the card sits idle for about 330. The README did not say so when this page's last entry was written. Its speed lane now reads 2 to 12, and the estimate is unchanged ahead of its next routine review. BRVIctory-ka1qux's README says the game's own ray-traced light now runs as an option on a Radeon RX 7800 XT: shaded buildings, trees and characters get bounced light, at about 0.05 seconds more per frame, in three runs of 5, 6 and 11 minutes without a crash. events.title: A private build's developer says Rockstar wrote to him, and Flamingo logs a 24-minute session at 8.6 frames a second
events.note: A private build's developer says Rockstar wrote to him, and Flamingo logs a 24-minute session at 8.6 frames a second  VGTimes reports that the developer of the private build listed here as omonkey says he has received a letter from Rockstar and has stopped streaming his work, while promising further updates. The letter has not been published and Rockstar has not commented. It is the first report of this kind seen here. Flamingo's run log reports a 24-minute play session through the whole opening and on into the city, at 8.6 frames a second on average in the world on an RTX 4070. That is the highest average reported from a session of 20 minutes or more, from one machine and unconfirmed, and it is under the 10 the next mark asks for. An open pull request against victory-fork reports the game's ray-tracing structure builder running whole through 7 minutes of play, kept off by default because it costs about 88 milliseconds a frame. VIniVIdiVIci moves from the watch list into the table at stage 5: its README reports the world at 3 to 5 frames a second on an RTX 4060 Ti, with no input tested yet. Forecast review: the estimate stays at the evening of Thu 26 Nov. The afternoon has brought more builds, a session from a new game into the open world and ray tracing as an experiment, but no figure above 14 in play, and victory-fork's main code has not moved since 12:43 UTC . News check: no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two, and no notice naming another project.     15:13  25 Nov

events.title: Stage 6 is now ordered by a published rule, and klbf-lab moves to first
events.note: Stage 6 is now ordered by a published rule, and klbf-lab moves to first  Until now the order inside a stage was this page's own judgement. From this check the 13 rows at stage 6 are ordered by their lanes and nothing else: fewest steps short of the playable bar on speed and stability together, then the better picture, the higher frame rate and the longer session. The key under the standings title states the rule, and each row shows its count. The rule reads only what projects report about themselves, on different cards and scenes, and it does not count how far into the story a build has been played. XCL's report adds a second, independent route into the game's world, but it gives no frame rate in play, no player control and no long runs. In the VIctory family, the best figure measured in play has been about 7.6 frames a second for over seven hours. A community-run board that tallies testers' reports on XCL's pull requests, last updated at 00:44 UTC , lists five reports of the world on screen and one of a tester playing by hand at about 6.9 frames a second in a short run. The board says these counts are not confirmed. What would move the estimate: earlier if XCL reports control, a frame rate in the world or a longer run, or if a speed gain is merged in the VIctory family; later if neither has happened by mid-morning in Europe. News check: no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two, no takedown notice naming another project, and no press coverage yet of XCL's report or of builds past the opening mission.     05:01  25 Nov

events.title: XCL reports its 3D world, at 14 frames a second on average over a short run
events.note: XCL reports its 3D world, at 14 frames a second on average over a short run  XCL's README, updated at 04:53 UTC , says that with a branch not yet merged the newer retail game it does not name goes on from its menus into its 3D world on an RTX 5090. It gives 4,307 frames in a 300-second run, which is 14 frames a second on average, and about 5 in the heaviest scene. The README does not split that run between the menus, which run at 30 frames a second, and the world, so 14 is not a frame rate in play. It calls the game not playable: the picture of the world is incomplete, with its minimap and other mesh pipelines refused, and it does not keep running there for long. It does not say whether the player has control. XCL is a separate code base from VIctory and its forks, so this is a second route into the game's world. It stays at stage 5 here until it reports control, and moves ahead of five-star-recomp. The estimate is unchanged for now and is due a routine review at about 05:30 UTC . The best figure measured in play is still about 7.6 frames a second, from the VIctory family.     04:20  25 Nov

events.title: Speed work in the pull-request queues: a large gain on a synthetic test, smaller ones measured in the game
events.note: Speed work in the pull-request queues: a large gain on a synthetic test, smaller ones measured in the game  An open pull request on victory-fork changes how the layer tracks the memory the game writes, and reports a drop from 390 ms to 9.8 ms a frame on an idle RTX 4090. That figure comes from a test program its author wrote, not from the game: the author says no game files were on the test PC. Its effect on the game has not been measured. Measured in the game: an open pull request on VIctory cuts the graphics time of a world frame on an RX 9070 XT under Proton from 600 to 720 ms down to 150 to 310 ms, and one on the fork takes an RTX 3070 laptop card in Series S mode from 353 ms to 305 ms a frame. None of these is merged, and none is a new top speed: the best measured figure in play is still about 7.6 frames a second. News check at 04:20 UTC : no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two, and no new takedown notice.     04:00  25 Nov

events.title: victory-fork's main branch moves again; estimate reviewed and held at about 2 days
events.note: victory-fork's main branch moves again; estimate reviewed and held at about 2 days  victory-fork's maintainer merged texture fixes at 03:19 UTC , the first change to its main branch in two hours. The notes say the first room now shows its walls and the characters' textures on a first launch, and put speed at about 3 to 5 frames a second. They add that more than half of the card's texture memory is held for detail levels the game has not loaded, which is the next job. Routine review of the estimate at 03:30 UTC : unchanged at about 2 days. Stability has three reports beyond the bar, so speed is the gap. The best measured figure in play has been about 7.6 frames a second for over five hours, most of them overnight in Europe, while more than 500 pull requests have now been opened against the fork. That is too short a pause to move the estimate later, and nothing has happened to move it earlier. One clue on speed for common cards: an open pull request on the fork measures the graphics time per frame in the first room at about three times higher on an 8 GB card once its texture memory runs out. Press: no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two has appeared in any coverage found. The Verge reported the Leonida takedown on 24 November, and by Make Tech Easier's account it names VIctory and its forks as the projects in front. Notebookcheck relays unverified Reddit claims that more Discord servers have been removed.     03:10  25 Nov

events.title: A public build reports the whole opening mission played, in a session of over 90 minutes
events.note: A public build reports the whole opening mission played, in a session of over 90 minutes  ztrx, a build of victory-fork's code published at 01:11 UTC on 25 November , reports in its README the opening mission playable from start to finish on an RTX 3050 with 8 GB, in one session of more than 1 hour 30 minutes without a crash. It runs at 1 to 3 frames a second, and anything in shadow is black. It is the first public code to make that claim and the longest session reported by anyone. PortWatch, which first listed it as a private build, says it verified the build going on into the next mission. A second public build of the same code, VItoriaBr, joins the standings. Its README reports the opening scenes at about 3 frames a second on an RTX 5060 Ti and says the world is not yet playable, while PortWatch reports its live stream reaching the second mission at up to 4 frames a second. victory-fork's main branch now runs at about 4.3 frames a second on an RTX 4070 by default, up from about 2.5, and lights its first room for the first time. The estimate moves in by a quarter of a day, to about 2 days: stability now has two long reports, and speed is the only gap left.     01:06  25 Nov

events.title: GitHub publishes a Take-Two takedown notice against Leonida and its forks
events.note: GitHub publishes a Take-Two takedown notice against Leonida and its forks  GitHub's public list of takedown notices now carries one from Take-Two, dated 24 November, against Leonida's repository. events.note: five-star-recomp fixes its memory corruption  five-star-recomp says the memory corruption in its story load is fixed. VIctory's main branch has had no commit since 09:53 UTC , while more than 1,000 pull requests have been opened against it. events.title: VIctory-Belobug-AMD shades its stand-in light, and IGN asks Take-Two for comment
events.note: VIctory-Belobug-AMD shades its stand-in light, and IGN asks Take-Two for comment  VIctory-Belobug-AMD's README (14:00 UTC) says its stand-in for ray-traced light is now weaker in creases and under objects, and that the game's own sun and lamp shadows work. It still reports 3 to 5 frames a second on a Radeon RX 9070 XT, says about 380 draws a frame are dropped, and says the frame is bound by the processor's work. VIctory-macOS reports its current code staying in the world for over 20 minutes without freezing on an M3 Max, at 0.1 to 0.2 frames a second. Nobody has reached gameplay on a Mac. News check: IGN has reported on the takedown and says it has asked Take-Two for comment. No statement from Rockstar or Take-Two has appeared since the build leaked, and GitHub's list shows no notice naming another project. VIniVIdiVIci, a fork of victory-fork checked on an RTX 4060 Ti, joins the watch list at a reader's request. Its README says it has not yet published results of its own in play. The estimate is unchanged at the evening of Thu 26 Nov.     14:01  25 Nov

events.title: Stage 6 is now ordered by a published rule, and klbf-lab moves to first
events.note: Stage 6 is now ordered by a published rule, and klbf-lab moves to first  Until now the order inside a stage was this page's own judgement. From this check the 13 rows at stage 6 are ordered by their lanes and nothing else: fewest steps short of the playable bar on speed and stability together, then the better picture, the higher frame rate and the longer session. The key under the standings title states the rule, and each row shows its count. Speed is now read as the middle of the frame rates a project reports in play, where it was the best of them, so a best-case scene no longer sets the step. victory-perf's 4.5 to 14 reads as step 3 of 6, down from 4, and VItoriaBr's 3.5 to 6 as step 2, down from 3. The order today: klbf-lab, victory-fork, AnyXboxX, ztrx, VIctory-Belobug-AMD, victory-perf, omonkey, victory-amd, suri, VItoriaBr, ScarlettPort, CGBJ and VIctory. klbf-lab and victory-fork are level at 2 steps short, and klbf-lab's picture is a step better. A project that reports no run length counts as having none, which is why VItoriaBr and ScarlettPort sit lower than before. The rule reads only what projects report about themselves, on different cards and scenes, and it does not count how far into the story a build has been played. Stages below 6 have no lanes and are still ordered by this page's reading.      See 118 earlier updates    13:04  25 Nov

events.title: Correction: victory-fork withdraws the 8.9 frames a second reported here, and gives 7 to 8
events.note: Correction: victory-fork withdraws the 8.9 frames a second reported here, and gives 7 to 8  At 12:20 UTC this page reported victory-fork's first room at 6.0 frames a second by default and 8.9 with a newer draw path. At 12:43 UTC the project withdrew both figures: its README says the two runs stood in different scenes and could not be compared. Its corrected figures come from one run each on an RTX 4070. At the same load a frame takes 145 ms with the newer path off and 124 ms with it on and memory copies made in place, about 6.9 and 8.1 frames a second. It reached the open world and lost the graphics device there in about 13 minutes, with the 12 GB card out of room for new textures, and the cause is not known. The estimate does not move: the gain is smaller than first stated, ordinary play is still under 10 frames a second, and nothing was withdrawn as unstable. events.title: Estimate held at its mid-morning review
events.note: Estimate held at its mid-morning review  The mid-morning review leaves the estimate at early on Fri 27 Nov. This was the check for moving it a quarter of a day later if speed had not moved. It has started to: victory-fork merged its first frame-rate work at 07:30 UTC, and its notes name the cost that remains and a change that more than halves it but is not yet stable. What moves it next. Earlier by a quarter of a day: a second report of 10 or more in play, a confirmation of victory-perf's figures by someone else, or a measured gain in frame time merged into victory-fork. Later by a quarter of a day: those figures withdrawn or contradicted, or none of the three by the review at about 13:30 UTC. News check: nothing new. Neither Rockstar nor Take-Two has commented since the build leaked. Today's coverage, heise's included, reports the Leonida takedown from the notice GitHub published. events.note: VIctory-macOS reports the game world on screen on a Mac  VIctory-macOS's README, changed at 08:25 UTC, says that in a later run on one tester's M3 Max the game world appeared on screen before the game's own watchdog stopped it, with frames taking up to 28 seconds while shaders compiled. It is this project's first report of the world on screen on a Mac. It says nothing about control, so it stays at stage 5 and moves up one place to 13th, and the README still says the game is not playable on the Mac. Nothing has moved at the front. victory-fork's main branch is unchanged since 07:30 UTC, VIctory's since 01:36 UTC and XCL's world branch since 07:45 UTC. New pull-request measurements on victory-fork stay at about 4 frames a second on an RTX 3090 Ti, and victory-perf's figures are still unconfirmed.     08:17  25 Nov

events.title: ScarlettPort joins the table, and a second reduced-resolution measurement comes in under 7 frames a second
events.note: ScarlettPort joins the table, and a second reduced-resolution measurement comes in under 7 frames a second  ScarlettPort, a public build of victory-fork's code that this page had not listed, reports the lit world at about 3 to 4 frames a second on an RTX 3060 at reduced resolution, with the keyboard walking the character. Its README does not name the title and says nobody has played a session end to end. It enters the table at stage 6 in sixth place. victory-perf credits it for some of its code. A victory-fork pull request measured the game's lower-resolution mode on an RTX 3090 Ti: 6.1 to 6.4 frames a second, steady, in the opening mission, against 4.7 to 4.8 at full resolution. That supports the direction of victory-perf's report but not its 9 to 14, which nobody else has confirmed. The estimate does not move. News check: neither Rockstar nor Take-Two has commented since the build leaked. TweakTown's report that the Leonida takedown is confirmed rests on the notice GitHub published, and no notice names another project. GameGPU describes footage, credited to a post on X, of boat gameplay on open water at 3 to 5 frames a second, which matches what builds listed here report. No outlet has tested or covered victory-perf. XCL's unmerged world branch gained 17 commits on memory mapping and device handling, with no new frame rate, run length or word on control. victory-fork's main branch has not moved since 07:30 UTC and VIctory's since 01:36 UTC.     07:54  25 Nov

events.note: A new fork reports 9 to 14 frames a second in interiors, and victory-fork merges its first frame-rate work  victory-perf, a fork of victory-fork published on the morning of 25 November, reports the opening mission's interiors under player control at 9 to 14 frames a second on an RTX 4070 SUPER, and 4.5 to 6.5 in heavy scenes. The figures are its maintainer's own, from one machine at reduced resolution, with no run length given and shadows lit by stand-ins, and its heavy-scene figure matches what AnyXboxX already reports on the same card. It enters the table at stage 6 in fifth place until someone else confirms it. It calls those scenes playable, which they are not by this page's bar of 20 frames a second held for 30 minutes. victory-fork's maintainer merged the fork's first frame-rate work at 07:30 UTC. One processor-side pass fell from 70 to 220 ms a frame to about 3, but the frame is still 250 to 380 ms on an RTX 4070 because, in the README's words, "the card is the limit now". A change the maintainer tried cut the card's time from 100 to 150 ms a frame to 35 to 80, lost the graphics device twice and was left out. The estimate stays at early on Fri 27 Nov. These are the first signs of speed moving since 22:15 UTC on 24 November, but the best figure from a long run is still about 7.6 frames a second and the new ones are unconfirmed. events.title: Take-Two is reported to be sending takedown notices over footage of unofficial builds
events.note: Take-Two is reported to be sending takedown notices over footage of unofficial builds  VGTimes and Twisted Voxel report, citing a post on X by the reporter Ben, that Take-Two is sending takedown notices over social media posts that show footage of unofficial PC builds. By VGTimes' account, one notice says the port is being developed from leaked copies of Rockstar's files and that the footage contains Rockstar's characters, environments and other material. Neither report names a platform, a number of notices or a project, and neither carries a statement from Take-Two. It is the first reported action since the notice against Leonida. No new notice has appeared in GitHub's public list. Neither company has commented since the build leaked. Before launch, Take-Two's chief executive said piracy would be met with legal and technical measures, and called unofficial PC ports made with AI a creative concern more than a financial one. Projects: XCL's world branch has 12 more commits and no new figures. Two victory-fork pull requests report every ray-traced shadow program now translating, which is not yet ray-traced lighting in the game. Speed is unchanged.     06:01  25 Nov

events.title: XCL reports its 3D world, at 14 frames a second on average over a short run
events.note: XCL reports its 3D world, at 14 frames a second on average over a short run  XCL's README, updated at 04:53 UTC, says that with a branch not yet merged the newer retail game it does not name goes on from its menus into its 3D world on an RTX 5090. It gives 4,307 frames in a 300-second run, which is 14 frames a second on average, and about 5 in the heaviest scene. The README does not split that run between the menus, which run at 30 frames a second, and the world, so 14 is not a frame rate in play. It calls the game not playable: the picture of the world is incomplete, with its minimap and other mesh pipelines refused, and it does not keep running there for long. It does not say whether the player has control. XCL is a separate code base from VIctory and its forks, so this is a second route into the game's world. It stays at stage 5 here until it reports control, and moves ahead of five-star-recomp. The estimate is unchanged for now and is due a routine review at about 05:30 UTC. The best figure measured in play is still about 7.6 frames a second, from the VIctory family.     04:20  25 Nov

events.title: Speed work in the pull-request queues: a large gain on a synthetic test, smaller ones measured in the game
events.note: Speed work in the pull-request queues: a large gain on a synthetic test, smaller ones measured in the game  An open pull request on victory-fork changes how the layer tracks the memory the game writes, and reports a drop from 390 ms to 9.8 ms a frame on an idle RTX 4090. That figure comes from a test program its author wrote, not from the game: the author says no game files were on the test PC. Its effect on the game has not been measured. Measured in the game: an open pull request on VIctory cuts the graphics time of a world frame on an RX 9070 XT under Proton from 600 to 720 ms down to 150 to 310 ms, and one on the fork takes an RTX 3070 laptop card in Series S mode from 353 ms to 305 ms a frame. None of these is merged, and none is a new top speed: the best measured figure in play is still about 7.6 frames a second. News check at 04:20 UTC: no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two, and no new takedown notice.     04:00  25 Nov

events.title: XSXEmu starts the game's code on a Mac without Wine; correction on TuxBox's stage
events.note: XSXEmu starts the game's code on a Mac without Wine; correction on TuxBox's stage  XSXEmu's README now says the game's own code runs under Rosetta on Apple Silicon, starts its worker threads and opens its archives. It has not created a graphics device, run a shader or produced a frame, and it says no game is playable. It stays on the watch list. Correction: the 02:09 UTC update said TuxBox stays at stage 4. TuxBox has been at stage 5 on this page since 23 November, when it showed the player-selection prompt, and the standings showed stage 5 throughout. The earlier line is fixed. Nothing new on speed. victory-fork's main branch has not changed since 03:19 UTC, and VIctory's has not changed since 01:36 UTC. More than 510 pull requests have now been opened against the fork, and a new one reports and fixes a fault that ran parts of the ray-tracing structure builder up to 64 times more than asked.     03:32  25 Nov
events.analysis: 涉及运行稳定性；需要核对持续时长及是否发生崩溃。

events.title: victory-fork's main branch moves again; estimate reviewed and held at about 2 days
events.note: victory-fork's main branch moves again; estimate reviewed and held at about 2 days  victory-fork's maintainer merged texture fixes at 03:19 UTC, the first change to its main branch in two hours. The notes say the first room now shows its walls and the characters' textures on a first launch, and put speed at about 3 to 5 frames a second. They add that more than half of the card's texture memory is held for detail levels the game has not loaded, which is the next job. Routine review of the estimate at 03:30 UTC: unchanged at about 2 days. Stability has three reports beyond the bar, so speed is the gap. The best measured figure in play has been about 7.6 frames a second for over five hours, most of them overnight in Europe, while more than 500 pull requests have now been opened against the fork. That is too short a pause to move the estimate later, and nothing has happened to move it earlier. One clue on speed for common cards: an open pull request on the fork measures the graphics time per frame in the first room at about three times higher on an 8 GB card once its texture memory runs out. Press: no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two has appeared in any coverage found. The Verge reported the Leonida takedown on 24 November, and by Make Tech Easier's account it names VIctory and its forks as the projects in front. Notebookcheck relays unverified Reddit claims that more Discord servers have been removed.     03:10  25 Nov
events.analysis: 涉及权利人或平台措施；以公开原始通知为准。

events.title: Scarlight narrows to Linux on AMD and restates its speed; a fork joins the watch list
events.note: Scarlight narrows to Linux on AMD and restates its speed; a fork joins the watch list  Scarlight's README now describes it as a port for Linux on AMD RX 9000 cards first, and says it does not support NVIDIA cards or native Windows. Its candidate build, on victory-fork's code, shows the opening mission's world lit at 2 to 3 frames a second at best on an RX 9070 XT, with many runs at 1 to 2. The earlier README said about 1 to 4. The build is not merged into its main branch. Added to the watch list: project-flamingo, a fork of VIctory that Scarlight's README points NVIDIA and Windows users to. Its README still carries VIctory's status from 23 November and reports no results of its own. An open pull request against victory-fork reports all 52 programs of the game's ray-tracing structure builder translating on an RTX 3060 laptop card, up from 49. Its author says the builder then writes outside its buffers and the game faults, so ray-traced lighting is still missing. PortWatch now ranks ztrx first on its board, saying the build has not crashed between the opening mission and the second. Speed is unchanged everywhere: about 7.6 frames a second at best in play.     02:49  25 Nov
events.analysis: 涉及运行稳定性；需要核对持续时长及是否发生崩溃。

events.title: AnyXboxX's maintainer sees 7 to 8 frames a second in cutscenes
events.note: AnyXboxX's maintainer sees 7 to 8 frames a second in cutscenes  AnyXboxX's README now says its maintainer saw a steady 7 to 8 frames a second during cutscenes, with peaks at 9, read from the window caption on an RTX 4070 SUPER. In one scripted run the medians measured from the log were lower, at 2 to 3 frames a second depending on the scene. These are cutscene figures, and the two methods disagree. Its measured figure for the world under player control is unchanged at 5.3 to 6.9, so the top measured speed in play stays at about 7.6 frames a second and the estimate does not move. Nothing else changed in status. victory-fork's main branch has not moved since 01:22 UTC while more than 470 pull requests have been opened against it, VIctory's main branch has not moved since 01:36 UTC, and Palmwave remains unreachable.      See 94 earlier updates    02:29  25 Nov

events.title: AnyXboxX relays a report of the first two missions completed
events.note: AnyXboxX relays a report of the first two missions completed  AnyXboxX's README now says a contributor played for about 45 minutes at about 2 frames a second and completed the first two missions. The maintainer relays the report and did not measure it from the project's own logs. The maintainer reports every cutscene playing in full, and measures 5.3 to 6.9 frames a second on an RTX 4070 SUPER with its newest mix of victory-fork and fifteen of that project's pull requests. The mix no longer needs the Microsoft library it tried earlier. Ray-traced lighting is still off, and some graphics are missing in places. It is the furthest into the game that any public project has reported. Speed at the top is unchanged: about 7.6 frames a second at best, against the 20 that playable needs, so the estimate stays where it is.     02:09  25 Nov

events.title: TuxBox gets into the story intro on Linux
events.note: TuxBox gets into the story intro on Linux  TuxBox, which is not built on VIctory, reports a Linux run under Proton getting into the story intro by the game's own state after 9 minutes 41 seconds, then crashing. Until now it had stopped at the player selection prompt. It says the game is not playable: many shaders are unsupported, and the picture, input and frame times in the intro are not yet checked. It stays at stage 5 here, where it has been since it showed the player-selection prompt on 23 November. This line first said stage 4 and was corrected at 04:00 UTC on 25 November. No new speed figures elsewhere. More than 430 pull requests have now been opened against victory-fork, whose main branch has not changed since 01:22 UTC.     01:49  25 Nov

events.title: VIctory's main branch gets a speed change; correction on palmetto's origins
events.note: VIctory's main branch gets a speed change; correction on palmetto's origins  VIctory's maintainer merged a change at 01:36 UTC that stops the runtime re-checking memory the game's shaders did not write. Its notes put the old cost at 0.45 to 0.7 seconds of a 1.5 to 1.7 second frame in the opening cutscene. The README's figure of 1 to 2 seconds a frame is not yet updated. Correction: palmetto's commit history, public again since about 01:45 UTC, says the repository descends from the project network that received Take-Two's notice, and that references to the game and to that project were removed in response. This page said at 22:22 UTC that its files did not show that origin. five-star-recomp reports most of the opening cutscene's 3D passes now running. Its 3D world is still not visible, and long runs end in a GPU hang. Open pull requests on victory-fork and VIctory report fixes that let the game's ray-tracing structure builder run on NVIDIA cards and that restore material colours that came out black. Neither is merged.     01:28  25 Nov
events.analysis: 涉及运行稳定性；需要核对持续时长及是否发生崩溃。

events.title: A public build reports the whole opening mission played, in a session of over 90 minutes
events.note: A public build reports the whole opening mission played, in a session of over 90 minutes  ztrx, a build of victory-fork's code published at 01:11 UTC on 25 November, reports in its README the opening mission playable from start to finish on an RTX 3050 with 8 GB, in one session of more than 1 hour 30 minutes without a crash. It runs at 1 to 3 frames a second, and anything in shadow is black. It is the first public code to make that claim and the longest session reported by anyone. PortWatch, which first listed it as a private build, says it verified the build going on into the next mission. A second public build of the same code, VItoriaBr, joins the standings. Its README reports the opening scenes at about 3 frames a second on an RTX 5060 Ti and says the world is not yet playable, while PortWatch reports its live stream reaching the second mission at up to 4 frames a second. victory-fork's main branch now runs at about 4.3 frames a second on an RTX 4070 by default, up from about 2.5, and lights its first room for the first time. The estimate moves in by a quarter of a day, to about 2 days: stability now has two long reports, and speed is the only gap left.     01:06  25 Nov
events.analysis: 涉及运行稳定性；需要核对持续时长及是否发生崩溃。

events.title: Estimate reviewed and left at about 2½ days
events.note: Estimate reviewed and left at about 2½ days  The estimate was reviewed at 01:05 UTC on 25 November and is unchanged: about 2½ days, around midday on Fri 27 Nov. The highest reported rate has not moved since 22:15 UTC, about 7.6 frames a second on an RTX 4090, while mid-range cards have caught up to 6 or 7. Playable needs 20. PortWatch now says it has verified one private build playing through the opening mission into the next, at about 2 frames a second with poor rendering. That speaks to how well the game runs, not how fast, so it does not move the estimate. No takedown notice names a front-runner. Palmwave's repository has been unreachable for nearly three hours, for reasons that are not known.     00:46  25 Nov
events.analysis: 涉及权利人或平台措施；以公开原始通知为准。

events.title: PortWatch reports private builds getting past the opening mission
events.note: PortWatch reports private builds getting past the opening mission  PortWatch's owner reports that several private builds now play through the opening mission and load the next one, the furthest into the story anyone has reported. The report names no builds and cites no recordings, and says most appear to build on victory-fork. By the same report most of them still render the world badly and vehicles mostly do not work, so the next mission cannot be played properly. PortWatch has not changed its scores, and no public project claims this. victory-fork's main branch gained a fix for characters' faces and hair that came out black or pale in about three launches of four. The cause was textures uploaded before the game had filled them. Its README is unchanged.     00:26  25 Nov

events.title: VIctory merges about 130 pull requests, and Scarlight shows a lit picture on Linux
events.note: VIctory merges about 130 pull requests, and Scarlight shows a lit picture on Linux  VIctory's maintainer merged about 130 pull requests into its main branch between 00:20 and 00:23 UTC on 25 November, the first movement there in nearly three hours. Its status line is unchanged: the world is drawn at 1 to 2 seconds a frame, unlit. Its limits, by its own description: one machine with a top-end graphics card, most letters missing from the menu body text, 7 to 28 frames per second in the menus, tests not run, and nothing seen past the menus. It is not merged or reviewed. The video noted in the last update matches it. The pull request says one later screen came out as a single solid colour, and that colour is the exact green seen in the video. Forecast pulled in to about 3 days.     20:11  23 Nov

events.title: Leonida is further on than its main branch shows
events.note: Leonida is further on than its main branch shows  Leonida: pull requests that are still waiting to be merged show one contributor's build reaching the game's frame loop, with black frames and stand-in pipelines, and another working out why the first interface draw shows nothing. Leonida moves to stage 4. This page now reads Leonida's open pull requests as well as its main branch. Leonida: a pull request adds a notice that the project is moving its git hosting to its own server. The official repository was not there yet at 20:10 UTC. The main branch on GitHub has merged nothing since 18:54 UTC. five-star-recomp: rectangle lists fixed and the frame loop is now stable at 30 frames per second in two-minute runs. Frames are still black, and the project says the game is waiting in an early splash or loading state. Unverified sighting: a screen-share video shows a near-empty first screen with controller prompts, a plain green screen for a few seconds, then the game's legal notices menu. The details fit a real early boot, including Xbox prompts and the green of a movie playing with empty frames. No repository has claimed it, so no project is credited and no stage moves. XCL: no commits on its main branch since 18:11 UTC.     19:57  23 Nov

events.title: ZETTROX's GTA VI build looks uncrashable so far
events.note: ['ZETTROX\'s build of GTA VI hasn\'t crashed yet. It has played from Lucia\'s prologue into Jason\'s first mission, "Gone Fishing", where it showed the first kill with a gun in GTA VI on PC, and it hasn\'t gone down once along the way. Its README reports more than an hour and a half in one session without a crash.', 'That\'s rare this early. Running a game built for other hardware usually means crashing, and often. ZETTROX\'s is the only build on our board rated better than "Crashes sometimes": on Wednesday its stability went from 0.5 to 0.8 ("Rarely crashes"), which puts it first at 64.2%.', "It's also slowly getting toward free roam, the point where the story lets go and the open world is yours. That takes patience: the build runs at 1 to 3 frames per second, and the picture is still poor, with anything in shadow drawn black and bright scenes overexposed.", "What keeps it running isn't clear yet. Like Uilian's VItoriaBr, it's based on VIctory and hyphennn's victory-fork, with ZETTROX's own work for NVIDIA cards, tested on an RTX 3050. Unlike most builds this far along, its code is public, as Zettrox/ztrx, so anyone can compare it with victory-fork and find what's different."]
events.analysis: 涉及运行稳定性；需要核对持续时长及是否发生崩溃。

events.title: GTA VI builds clear Lucia's prologue and reach Jason's first mission
events.note: ['Several private PC builds of GTA VI can now play through Lucia\'s prologue and carry on into Jason\'s first mission, "Gone Fishing". Until now, the furthest builds we track had only reached the prologue itself, so this is the deepest into the story anyone has reported.', "It's rough. Most builds still render the world badly, and vehicles don't work most of the time: in Gone Fishing the boat often can't be steered. On some builds, the map in the pause menu opens.", "We can't say yet whose builds these are. The people getting this far are working in private, and most of them appear to build on hyphennn's victory-fork, the public fork of VIctory behind the top of our board. Their own changes aren't public, so nobody else can test them.", '"Prologue cleared" is the first step of our story track, but no score changes until we know which builds did it. If yours is one of them, open an issue on our GitHub with a link to a recording or a stream.']

events.title: We've seen Belobug's AMD build, and it's way ahead
events.note: ["We've seen Belobug's build of GTA VI running, and the PortWatch team thinks it's way ahead of every other build we track. The open world renders lit, with textures, people, vehicles, vegetation, water and sky, and it looks close to the retail game, just very slowly. It plays through missions, and it rarely crashes.", 'It went straight to #1 on our board at 77.4%, more than 13 points clear of ZETTROX\'s 64.2%, which led until this morning. Its rendering is rated 0.85 on our scale, the highest we\'ve given any build, and its story progress 0.5 ("First act"). The next best picture, suri\'s private build, is at 0.8; ZETTROX\'s, which draws anything in shadow black, is at 0.3.', "It's built for AMD Radeon, while ZETTROX's, the previous leader, is tuned for NVIDIA. Belobug runs it on a Radeon RX 9070 XT 16 GB with a Ryzen 7 9800X3D, 64 GB of RAM and Windows 11. It's a fork of Marvis's VIctory, following its main branch plus upstream pull requests, and its README says no code from hyphennn's victory-fork is in it. Belobug's own fixes include a stand-in for the game's ray-traced indirect light, which left leaves magenta and indoor scenes in coloured blocks, a fix for lines along every triangle on car paint, glass and skin, and a change that cut the GPU time of one heavy scene from 225 to about 80 milliseconds a frame.", 'It isn\'t fast. events.title: Take-Two's first GTA VI port takedown disables Leonida and 3,007 forks
events.note: ['Take-Two has filed its first DMCA notice against a GTA VI port. The notice, published in GitHub\'s public DMCA log on Tuesday, names ItsNotRexed\'s Leonida repository. Because the fork network was larger than 100 repositories and Take-Two said the forks infringe just as the original does, GitHub processed it against the whole network: 3,007 repositories. Contributor forks that survived Leonida\'s shutdown on Monday now show GitHub\'s "unavailable" page.', 'The publisher calls Leonida a derivative work of GTA VI and says it breaches the reverse-engineering ban in Rockstar\'s terms of service. It also argues that the project\'s "bring your own files" line is misleading: given the timing, it says, the files users must supply can only be the leaked Xbox build.', "The notice names only Leonida. Projects that aren't GitHub forks of it, such as VIctory and XCL, and Leonida copies uploaded as new repositories, are still online for now. But the same argument could apply to any of them.", 'Leonida stays on our board as nuked, for the record.']
events.analysis: 涉及权利人或平台措施；以公开原始通知为准。

events.title: PortWatch's new scale: Playable is halfway, finishing the game is 100%
events.note: ['We\'ve changed how PortWatch scores projects. The old bar climbed from groundwork to "In-game", then to 30 FPS and "Stable". Many of you pointed out that this mixed up two different things: getting the game to run at all, and having it play well. Walking around a dark world at 5 frames per second isn\'t three-quarters of the way to playing GTA VI on PC.', 'Getting in is now a ladder to 50%. Groundwork fills the first 10%. Then come Exe runs (10%), First frame (20%), Main menu (30%), In the world (40%), when story mode loads the world and draws it, however broken, and Playable (50%), when you control a character in it.', 'Past Playable, four tracks fill the other half side by side: story progress (35 points), from stuck in the opening to 100% completion; rendering (25), from black or broken to matching the console; performance (20), the average frame rate divided by 30; and stability (20). 100% now means the whole game can be finished, looking like the console, at 30 fps or better, without crashing.', "Every project has been re-scored, and the numbers are lower. The furthest builds are now just past halfway: hyphennn's private build at 59.4%, omonkey's at 57.9%, victory-gta6 at 57.3% and CGBJ's at 54.5%. VIctory is at 40%, in the world but not yet playable, and XCL at 35%. Nobody went backwards: the same results now count for less of the whole game.", 'The history chart has been converted to the new scale too. events.title: GTA VI's shaders start loading on omonkey's build, streamed live on Rumble
events.note: ["A developer called omonkey has GTA VI running on PC with its shaders starting to load properly. It runs at about 5 frames per second and is stuck in the opening scene, Lucia's prison, but a player can move around in it, slowly.", 'That puts omonkey ahead of every project we track. CGBJ, which we added earlier on Tuesday, also has a player moving, but on a black screen, and a video of it shows the opening in flat colours without lighting.', "omonkey streams all of his development work on Rumble, but not on a channel of his own. The streams go out on Swaggely, a channel with about 1,800 followers that belongs to a separate person. It isn't clear why the two work this way.", "We've added omonkey to the tracker at 76%, at our In-game stage, which puts him first. Because the work has been streamed live the whole time, we're confident it's real. We haven't found any public code from him, though, so nobody can test it outside the streams yet.", "Update, 20:10 UTC: omonkey's build is based on victory-gta6, fxceless's public fork of VIctory, which we've now added to the race at 74%. Our race now ranks only projects with public code, so omonkey's private build is listed below it without a rank. At 76% it still leads our overall progress number, and it shows on victory-gta6's card as a build on that code."]

events.title: Exclusive: CGBJ gets GTA VI in game, walking and talking in an unlit world
events.note: ['A group called CGBJ has got GTA VI into its game world on PC, and a player can move in it. With a controller they walk around, talk to NPCs and open the in-game menu. PortWatch has verified that it gets in game. No public project has shown a player moving yet.', "It is far from playable, and it runs very slowly. In the run where a player walked around, the screen was black. A 77-second video posted on X on Tuesday shows more: GTA VI's opening scenes in flat colours with no lighting, from a car's interior to a street of waving NPCs, a guard and a prison yard.", "CGBJ's code is private. It builds on VIctory, the open-source layer whose author first showed GTA VI's menus on a livestream on Monday, and also takes some of XCL's work. Both are public on GitHub; CGBJ's changes aren't, so nobody outside the group can test them.", "We've added CGBJ to the tracker at 72%, at our In-game stage, which puts it first. That rests on our own check: the video doesn't name the project, and nobody outside the group can reproduce the result yet.", "Update, 20:10 UTC: our race now ranks only projects with public code, so CGBJ's private build is listed below it without a rank, still at 72%. It counts toward our overall progress number, which omonkey's private build now leads at 76%, and it shows on the cards of VIctory and XCL as a build on their code."]

events.title: Exclusive: XCL reports 30 fps in GTA VI but won't say if it's past the menus
events.note: ["XCL says GTA VI now runs at 30 frames per second in game, but won't say where. Asked whether that means the menus it had already reached or actual gameplay, the team refused to answer, saying it feared being nuked. Privately, it hinted to one of our community members that things are working really well.", 'Its public notes haven\'t caught up. XCL\'s README still calls the game "a newer retail game" that reaches its menus at a steady 30 fps, with gameplay not reached yet. Early on Tuesday the project merged a change that shows the live frame rate in the game window\'s title.', "The caution runs through the scene. XCL's Discord server is tightly locked down with its chats closed, and members are scared of being nuked after Leonida lost its server, its repository and its creator within an hour on Monday night. The GTA 6 Modding Discord server has now been nuked too.", 'Update, 01:50 UTC: testers on XCL\'s GitHub now report GTA VI getting past its menus into the world on the public code. The game\'s own state reads "Game Running", but the screen stays on a loading spinner and a GPU watchdog ends each run within minutes. One report claims gameplay at 28 to 30 fps, without a screenshot. XCL moves to 62.5%, halfway to In-game.']
events.analysis: 涉及运行稳定性；需要核对持续时长及是否发生崩溃。

events.title: TuxBox draws GTA VI's first screen as VIctory edges into the world
events.note: ["Leonida's exit hasn't slowed the other GTA VI ports. TuxBox, a compatibility layer tested mostly on Linux through Proton, published a run record showing the game's player-selection prompt at 4K on an RTX 4070 Ti SUPER. It hasn't sent the game any input yet, so we count it as a first frame, not a menu. That takes TuxBox from 25% to 40%.", "VIctory, level with XCL at the main menu, now says its runs reach the world. The first mission's title card renders, but the scene behind it stays dark at roughly one frame every one to two seconds, and the project warns that real GPUs can hang. That isn't playable, so VIctory stays at 55%.", 'PercyScarlett reports GTA VI running to a frame loop of black frames before the GPU hangs, and a new project, GTA6-BootTest, gets its exe through the same stage with stand-in DLLs. Both now sit at "Exe runs". As always, these are the projects\' own reports; none has been reproduced independently.']

events.title: Leonida is nuked: GitHub repo deleted, Discord gone, creator quits
events.note: ['Leonida, the most-starred GTA VI port with more than 33,000 GitHub stars, went offline in under an hour on Monday night. Its Discord server stopped resolving at about 23:07 UTC. By 23:47 its GitHub repository was gone. Around the same time its creator, NotRexed, posted "I quit guys" on X, writing that he kept running into problems he couldn\'t control and was stepping away, and thanking the Discord community.', 'The repository now answers "not found", not the "unavailable" page GitHub shows after a DMCA takedown, and GitHub\'s public DMCA log has no notice against it. That points to its owners pulling it rather than Take-Two, though only they can say. Earlier that evening it had moved to a new organization, ProjectLeonida, whose maintainers closed thousands of open pull requests and issues.', "The code isn't lost. Contributors' forks are still on GitHub, among them the one carrying the combined boot fixes, and a mirror on NotRexed's own Git server holds the code as of 23:30 UTC, though it can no longer sync.", "We've marked Leonida as nuked on the tracker. It stays on the board for the record but no longer counts in the rankings.", "Update, Nov 24: Take-Two has since filed a DMCA notice against Leonida, published in GitHub's log on Nov 24, and GitHub disabled the repository's whole network of 3,007 forks, including the contributor fork linked below. Copies uploaded as separate repositories are not part of that network."]
events.analysis: 涉及权利人或平台措施；以公开原始通知为准。

events.title: Leonida's Discord server disappears as the project moves to a new GitHub account
events.note: ["Leonida's Discord server went offline late on Monday. At 23:06 UTC its invite still led to a server of about 179,000 members, 74,000 of them online. Within a minute Discord answered that both the invite and the server were unknown. Members say Discord banned it. Neither Discord nor the Leonida team has said why, and from outside we can't tell a ban from a deletion.", "At first the code was untouched. About an hour earlier the repository had moved from its creator's personal account to a new organization, ProjectLeonida, created at 22:08 UTC. Old links redirected, and issues were still being updated after the server went dark. Around the same time the maintainers closed thousands of open pull requests and issues, cutting the list from nearly 4,900 to about 200.", "GitHub's public DMCA log shows no notice against the project. The disappearance follows other pressure on GTA VI communities: earlier this month the GTA 6 Mapping Project's Discord vanished without explanation, and in August Take-Two sought subpoenas against Discord to identify the leaker, which Discord said it hadn't been served.", 'Update, 23:47 UTC: the GitHub repository has since been deleted, and its creator says he has quit. See our follow-up.']
events.analysis: 涉及权利人或平台措施；以公开原始通知为准。

events.title: Exclusive: Marvis livestreams GTA VI reaching its menus at about 15 fps
events.note: ["A developer who goes by Marvis livestreamed GTA VI running on a PC on Monday, getting as far as the game's menus at roughly 15 frames per second. No public project has shown that much yet: Leonida, XCL and TuxBox all run the game's own code, but their screens are still black or blank.", "Late on Monday he published the code on GitHub as VIctory, a Rust layer that runs the game's own code natively on Windows. Its README goes further than the stream: boot screens, intro video, start screen and saves work at 30 fps, and loading reaches the open world, where the picture stays black and the graphics card fails within seconds.", "Viewers who went through the stream closely mostly concluded it is genuine. A staged fake would take a very elaborate setup, and few think that is what happened. The timing also fits: an outside contributor's unmerged change to XCL reports reaching the first menus on the same day.", "VIctory sits at our Main menu stage, 55%. Its results are still his own, from one PC with an AMD RX 6700 XT; we'll update the entry as others try the code, and take it down if the run turns out to be staged."]
events.analysis: 涉及运行稳定性；需要核对持续时长及是否发生崩溃。

events.title: Leonida gets GTA VI's executable running, but nothing is on screen yet
events.note: ["Hours after Cyberleek's executable appeared on Monday, Leonida's contributors began running it through the project's runtime and logging each attempt in a shared issue. On builds that stack about 25 unmerged pull requests, the retail executable now runs its own code for up to three minutes on Windows, Wine and Proton. It sets up the graphics device, gets through audio setup, builds tens of thousands of graphics pipelines and opens a window.", "That window stays blank. The current wall is a console-only call on the game's command allocators that the PC layer doesn't answer, so frames never finish. None of the boot fixes are in Leonida's main branch yet, and contributors call merging them the bottleneck.", 'Posts in Leonida\'s Discord server told the same story. Soon after the drop, one said the game won\'t be playable today, "but maybe tomorrow". Later, another said it "almost boots", with a black screen and audio that cuts off. We can\'t check that timeline, and the repo still lists input, saves and streaming as not started.', "Leonida isn't alone. XCL runs a retail game its notes identify by GTA VI's executable at 30 fps on a black screen, and TuxBox shows the same black window on Proton. All three now sit at our Exe runs stage, 25%. None has drawn a picture."]

events.title: Cyberleek's README frames the leak as a protest and asks for crypto
events.note: ["A text file said to be the README from Cyberleek's archive was shared on Reddit on Nov 23, shortly after the executable drop. We haven't seen the archive ourselves, so we can't confirm the note is genuine. Here is everything it says, in our words.", 'It casts the leaks as a fight against what it calls anti-consumer habits in games: subscriptions added to single-player titles, pricey special editions that only unlock content already in the files, and licences sold as if they were purchases. Its own summary: "The enemy is the tactic, not the game." It says players were never the target, which is why the ending and story were kept out of the leaks, and that every release since its first clip in August 2026 has cost nothing.', "Then it turns defiant. It claims months of takedowns, subpoenas and wallet tracing haven't stopped the uploads, and argues that money can't make any protection unbreakable and courts can't pull back what has already spread online.", "Next comes the money. The note says donations fund a project it won't describe until there's something to show, and that some money has already arrived and paid for the first steps. It says the skills behind the build would earn more in other, quieter work, while insisting that isn't a threat. Backers, it says, can only change how fast that project becomes its main focus, not where it goes. It promises future releases will be free whether or not anyone pays, but counts every donation and every trade of its token as a vote.",
events.analysis: 涉及权利人或平台措施；以公开原始通知为准。

events.title: Cyberleek says the missing GTA VI executable is out, hours before its own deadline
events.note: ['Cyberleek posted on Monday, Nov 23 at 15:36 CET (14:36 UTC) that the executable missing from its leaked Xbox Series build of GTA VI is now out. That is about two and a half hours before the 18:00 CET deadline the leaker had set itself. The post calls the release free and says it hands the work over to the open-source recompilation and emulation projects.', "We haven't downloaded or checked the file, and we won't link to it. When we published, no outlet had confirmed it is genuine. The post also asks for crypto donations, and Cyberleek has tied earlier releases to a token, so treat the claims around it with care.", "Expect fakes. Leaked files are an easy way to spread malware, and fake GTA VI downloads were circulating before this drop. Don't run executables you got from strangers, and only use the original project repositories linked in the race on our homepage.", 'For the race, this is the starting gun: until now no project could even try to boot GTA VI. Nothing on the tracker changes until one shows it running, and the countdown on our homepage now counts up from the release.']

events.title: AnyPS5 developer suspended on X, with no evidence Sony or Rockstar was behind it
events.note: ["The X account of boykopovar, the developer of PS5-to-PC tool AnyPS5, is suspended. We saw the notice on the profile on Nov 22. It points to X's rules in general and doesn't say which one was broken or whether anyone complained.", "An account describing itself as AnyPS5's community account called it a repeat suspension and suggested Sony and Rockstar fear the project. It showed no evidence that either company was involved, and we found no reporting or statement that says so. We couldn't confirm an earlier suspension either.", "AnyPS5 itself is still online: new code reached its GitHub repository later that day. One project we track, americas-recomp, is a fork of it. The suspension doesn't change any scores or show progress on running GTA VI.", "Be careful with what travels alongside this story. The account making the claim promotes a token using the project's name and says the developer supports it. We haven't verified that, and saw no mention of a token in the project's README or on the developer's public Telegram channel. Don't treat the suspension as a reason to buy one."]
events.analysis: 涉及运行稳定性；需要核对持续时长及是否发生崩溃。

events.title: XCL takes the lead after running its first retail Xbox games on PC
events.note: ["XCL runs Xbox Series code natively and swaps in its own versions of the console's system libraries. On Nov 22 its README began reporting that Minecraft Preview is fully playable on a PC, with worlds, sound and a controller. Fortnite and XDefiant reach their title screens and menus, going as far as they can without their online services.", "Its commit history over the day matches that account: Fortnite's splash screen in the morning, Minecraft's main menu by early afternoon and a playable build by the evening. The results are self-reported, and nobody else has reproduced them yet.", "For GTA VI, XCL says all 26,698 GPU programs in the game's shader pack translate to HLSL and that sampled ones compile for PC. Running another retail game end to end is the strongest sign yet that a layer like this could carry GTA VI. XCL's score rises to about 22%, ahead of xbox-emulator.", "Elsewhere, americas-recomp now translates almost all of the game's shaders, and Leonida's loader runs a stand-in program end to end. Every project is still waiting on the same file."]
events.analysis: 涉及画面输出；不代表完整图形管线或可玩性已解决。

events.title: The missing GTA VI executable is due Monday at 18:00 CET, and votes cost money
events.note: ['Cyberleek\'s own countdown for the withheld executable ends on Monday, Nov 23 at 18:00 CET (17:00 UTC), and RockstarINTEL reports the same deadline. That is more precise than the "Monday" first announced, and it is the time the countdown on this page now uses.', "The leaker's site pairs the timer with a poll on what happens next, and votes are cast by paying in cryptocurrency. RockstarINTEL also reports that the token goal for an early release has dropped to $6 million, after $30 million in October and $15 million earlier this week. Reports put the token at about $1.4 million.", "None of this is verified. No outlet has confirmed that the group holds a working executable, and Decrypt and others describe the countdown as a way to pump the token. The group ended a similar campaign in October when its goal wasn't met.", 'If a file does appear, expect fakes first. Security researchers have already found fake "GTA VI installers" carrying the Vidar info-stealer and hundreds of domains pushing fake launchers. This tracker will report a release only once outlets confirm it, and will never link to it.']

events.title: Re-uploads of the leading GTA VI projects are already circulating
events.note: ['Our scout ran for the first time on Saturday night. Among a dozen new repositories it found three that were not new projects at all: they were re-uploads of Leonida, the most-starred GTA VI port, published under unrelated accounts.', "Two kept the original name. The third had been renamed to something that sounds like GTA, carried a one-line description, and had a README that was 97% identical to Leonida's.", "A re-upload isn't necessarily malicious. Plenty of people mirror code they find interesting. But a copied repo is the easiest place to slip a modified build script or a fake executable into something that looks trustworthy, and Leonida is built by double-clicking a batch file.", "From today, the scout compares every new repository's README against the projects we track and flags close copies instead of listing them. Unreviewed repositories are no longer linked from this site. If you're following a project, use only the original repository linked in the race."]

events.title: Cyberleek's Xbox build is out, except the file that runs it
events.note: ["Cyberleek, the group behind this year's GTA VI footage leaks, says it has released a roughly 209 GB Xbox Series build of the game, labelled version 1.0.2.1, by torrent. The game's main executable is not included.", "According to the group's statement, the executable will be released on Monday, Nov 23, with no conditions attached. It says the file will come out immediately if its CYBERLEEK token reaches a $15 million market cap first.", 'No outlet or security researcher has independently verified that the files are a genuine GTA VI build, and Rockstar and Take-Two have not commented. Projects on this tracker say they are working with a package whose contents match what they expect, including 26,503 shaders, but none can boot it without the executable.', 'Cyberleek also predicted that PC players would be emulating the build within a week. As Gamereactor points out, no working Xbox Series X|S emulator exists yet. That gap is exactly what the projects on this page are trying to close.']
events.analysis: 涉及画面输出；不代表完整图形管线或可玩性已解决。

events.title: Every “GTA VI for PC” download is fake, and some empty your accounts
events.note: ["There is no PC version of GTA VI. Rockstar hasn't announced one, and no community port can run the game yet. That hasn't stopped a wave of fake installers.", 'Kaspersky has logged more than 27,000 detections of GTA VI-themed malware and unwanted software since June. ESET found a file named gta6_installer.exe carrying the Vidar infostealer. Cynet analysed a fake download that installs a stealer which takes saved passwords, browser cookies, Steam and Roblox logins and crypto wallet data.', 'NordVPN researchers also found a dark-web bundle selling for about $200 in crypto. It lets low-skill scammers run their own fake GTA VI download campaigns.', "The warning signs are consistent. Instructions ask you to run the file as administrator, click past security warnings or add an antivirus exclusion, and some offers ask for payment in crypto or gift cards. With Cyberleek's missing executable due Monday, expect a flood of files claiming to be it. If you've already run one, treat the PC as compromised and change your passwords from a different device."]

events.title: Take-Two hits GTA V ports on GitHub, saying “bring your own files” is no defence
events.note: ['On Nov 18, the day before GTA VI launched, Take-Two sent GitHub four DMCA takedown notices aimed at unofficial GTA V ports. The targets included an iOS and macOS port, a multi-platform runtime, an Android port, and repositories linked to a browser-based version.', "Reports differ on the scale. One counted 349 disabled forks of a single port, while another headline put the total above 600 projects. GitHub didn't publish a final count.", "The argument matters more than the numbers. Three of the four projects shipped no game files and told users to supply their own copy. Take-Two's notices argue that this setup doesn't excuse helping people reproduce the game without permission.", 'Every GTA VI project on this tracker uses the same “use your own copy” disclaimer. Developers can contest a takedown with a counter-notice, which obliges GitHub to restore the code unless Take-Two sues, as it did over the re3 and reVC projects in 2021.']

events.title: The 2022 GTA VI hacker pleads guilty and will be sentenced on Monday
events.note: ['Arion Kurtaj, the hacker behind the September 2022 leak of early GTA VI development footage, pleaded guilty at Woolwich Crown Court in London on Nov 16. He admitted hacking Rockstar Games and putting roughly 90 clips online.', 'The charges also cover intrusions at other companies. He is due to be sentenced at the same court on Monday, Nov 23, the same day Cyberleek says it will release the missing executable for its leaked Xbox build.', "The two leaks are separate. The 2022 breach exposed unfinished footage from inside Rockstar. Cyberleek's 2026 release claims to be a finished console build of the shipped game."]

after.title: ZETTROX's GTA VI build looks uncrashable so far
after.note: ['ZETTROX\'s build of GTA VI hasn\'t crashed yet. It has played from Lucia\'s prologue into Jason\'s first mission, "Gone Fishing", where it showed the first kill with a gun in GTA VI on PC, and it hasn\'t gone down once along the way. Its README reports more than an hour and a half in one session without a crash.', 'That\'s rare this early. Running a game built for other hardware usually means crashing, and often. ZETTROX\'s is the only build on our board rated better than "Crashes sometimes": on Wednesday its stability went from 0.5 to 0.8 ("Rarely crashes"), which puts it first at 64.2%.', "It's also slowly getting toward free roam, the point where the story lets go and the open world is yours. That takes patience: the build runs at 1 to 3 frames per second, and the picture is still poor, with anything in shadow drawn black and bright scenes overexposed.", "What keeps it running isn't clear yet. Like Uilian's VItoriaBr, it's based on VIctory and hyphennn's victory-fork, with ZETTROX's own work for NVIDIA cards, tested on an RTX 3050. Unlike most builds this far along, its code is public, as Zettrox/ztrx, so anyone can compare it with victory-fork and find what's different."]

after.title: GTA VI builds clear Lucia's prologue and reach Jason's first mission

Until now, the furthest builds we track had only reached the prologue itself, so this is the deepest into the story anyone has reported.', "It's rough. Most builds still render the world badly, and vehicles don't work most of the time: in Gone Fishing the boat often can't be steered. On some builds, the map in the pause menu opens.", "We can't say yet whose builds these are. Their own changes aren't public, so nobody else can test them.", '"Prologue cleared" is the first step of our story track, but no score changes until we know which builds did it. If yours is one of them, open an issue on our GitHub with a link to a recording or a stream.']

after.title: Take-Two's first GTA VI port takedown disables Leonida and 3,007 forks
after.note: ['Take-Two has filed its first DMCA notice against a GTA VI port. The notice, published in GitHub\'s public DMCA log on Tuesday, names ItsNotRexed\'s Leonida repository. Because the fork network was larger than 100 repositories and Take-Two said the forks infringe just as the original does, GitHub processed it against the whole network: 3,007 repositories. Contributor forks that survived Leonida\'s shutdown on Monday now show GitHub\'s "unavailable" page.', 'The publisher calls Leonida a derivative work of GTA VI and says it breaches the reverse-engineering ban in Rockstar\'s terms of service. It also argues that the project\'s "bring your own files" line is misleading: given the timing, it says, the files users must supply can only be the leaked Xbox build.', "The notice names only Leonida. Projects that aren't GitHub forks of it, such as VIctory and XCL, and Leonida copies uploaded as new repositories, are still online for now. But the same argument could apply to any of them.", 'Leonida stays on our board as nuked, for the record.']

Many of you pointed out that this mixed up two different things: getting the game to run at all, and having it play well. Walking around a dark world at 5 frames per second isn\'t three-quarters of the way to playing GTA VI on PC.', 'Getting in is now a ladder to 50%. Groundwork fills the first 10%. Then come Exe runs (10%), First frame (20%), Main menu (30%), In the world (40%), when story mode loads the world and draws it, however broken, and Playable (50%), when you control a character in it.', 'Past Playable, four tracks fill the other half side by side: story progress (35 points), from stuck in the opening to 100% completion; rendering (25), from black or broken to matching the console; performance (20), the average frame rate divided by 30; and stability (20). 100% now means the whole game can be finished, looking like the console, at 30 fps or better, without crashing.', "Every project has been re-scored, and the numbers are lower. The furthest builds are now just past halfway: hyphennn's private build at 59.4%, omonkey's at 57.9%, victory-gta6 at 57.3% and CGBJ's at 54.5%. VIctory is at 40%, in the world but not yet playable, and XCL at 35%. Nobody went backwards: the same results now count for less of the whole game.", 'The history chart has been converted to the new scale too. after.title: Exclusive: CGBJ gets GTA VI in game, walking and talking in an unlit world

In the run where a player walked around, the screen was black. A 77-second video posted on X on Tuesday shows more: GTA VI's opening scenes in flat colours with no lighting, from a car's interior to a street of waving NPCs, a guard and a prison yard.", "CGBJ's code is private. after.note: ["XCL says GTA VI now runs at 30 frames per second in game, but won't say where. Asked whether that means the menus it had already reached or actual gameplay, the team refused to answer, saying it feared being nuked. Privately, it hinted to one of our community members that things are working really well.", 'Its public notes haven\'t caught up. XCL\'s README still calls the game "a newer retail game" that reaches its menus at a steady 30 fps, with gameplay not reached yet. Early on Tuesday the project merged a change that shows the live frame rate in the game window\'s title.', "The caution runs through the scene. XCL's Discord server is tightly locked down with its chats closed, and members are scared of being nuked after Leonida lost its server, its repository and its creator within an hour on Monday night. The GTA 6 Modding Discord server has now been nuked too.", 'Update, 01:50 UTC: testers on XCL\'s GitHub now report GTA VI getting past its menus into the world on the public code. The game\'s own state reads "Game Running", but the screen stays on a loading spinner and a GPU watchdog ends each run within minutes. One report claims gameplay at 28 to 30 fps, without a screenshot. XCL moves to 62.5%, halfway to In-game.']

after.title: Leonida is nuked: GitHub repo deleted, Discord gone, creator quits
after.note: ['Leonida, the most-starred GTA VI port with more than 33,000 GitHub stars, went offline in under an hour on Monday night. Its Discord server stopped resolving at about 23:07 UTC. By 23:47 its GitHub repository was gone. Around the same time its creator, NotRexed, posted "I quit guys" on X, writing that he kept running into problems he couldn\'t control and was stepping away, and thanking the Discord community.', 'The repository now answers "not found", not the "unavailable" page GitHub shows after a DMCA takedown, and GitHub\'s public DMCA log has no notice against it. That points to its owners pulling it rather than Take-Two, though only they can say. Earlier that evening it had moved to a new organization, ProjectLeonida, whose maintainers closed thousands of open pull requests and issues.', "The code isn't lost. Contributors' forks are still on GitHub, among them the one carrying the combined boot fixes, and a mirror on NotRexed's own Git server holds the code as of 23:30 UTC, though it can no longer sync.", "We've marked Leonida as nuked on the tracker. It stays on the board for the record but no longer counts in the rankings.", "Update, Nov 24: Take-Two has since filed a DMCA notice against Leonida, published in GitHub's log on Nov 24, and GitHub disabled the repository's whole network of 3,007 forks, including the contributor fork linked below. Copies uploaded as separate repositories are not part of that network."]
after.analysis: 涉及权利人或平台措施；以公开原始通知为准。

after.title: Leonida's Discord server disappears as the project moves to a new GitHub account
after.note: ["Leonida's Discord server went offline late on Monday. At 23:06 UTC its invite still led to a server of about 179,000 members, 74,000 of them online. Within a minute Discord answered that both the invite and the server were unknown. Members say Discord banned it. Neither Discord nor the Leonida team has said why, and from outside we can't tell a ban from a deletion.", "At first the code was untouched. About an hour earlier the repository had moved from its creator's personal account to a new organization, ProjectLeonida, created at 22:08 UTC. Old links redirected, and issues were still being updated after the server went dark. Around the same time the maintainers closed thousands of open pull requests and issues, cutting the list from nearly 4,900 to about 200.", "GitHub's public DMCA log shows no notice against the project. The disappearance follows other pressure on GTA VI communities: earlier this month the GTA 6 Mapping Project's Discord vanished without explanation, and in August Take-Two sought subpoenas against Discord to identify the leaker, which Discord said it hadn't been served.", 'Update, 23:47 UTC: the GitHub repository has since been deleted, and its creator says he has quit. See our follow-up.']

after.title: Exclusive: Marvis livestreams GTA VI reaching its menus at about 15 fps
after.note: ["A developer who goes by Marvis livestreamed GTA VI running on a PC on Monday, getting as far as the game's menus at roughly 15 frames per second. No public project has shown that much yet: Leonida, XCL and TuxBox all run the game's own code, but their screens are still black or blank.", "Late on Monday he published the code on GitHub as VIctory, a Rust layer that runs the game's own code natively on Windows. Its README goes further than the stream: boot screens, intro video, start screen and saves work at 30 fps, and loading reaches the open world, where the picture stays black and the graphics card fails within seconds.", "Viewers who went through the stream closely mostly concluded it is genuine. A staged fake would take a very elaborate setup, and few think that is what happened. The timing also fits: an outside contributor's unmerged change to XCL reports reaching the first menus on the same day.", "VIctory sits at our Main menu stage, 55%. Its results are still his own, from one PC with an AMD RX 6700 XT; we'll update the entry as others try the code, and take it down if the run turns out to be staged."]
